info.name: ChampBeam API
info.description:
# ChampBeam API

Create **trackable short links** (with QR codes), host files behind trackable links, and read click analytics — from any application, under your own domain.

## Authentication

Create an API key in the ChampBeam app under **Settings → API keys**, then send it on every request in the `X-API-Key` header (an `Authorization: Bearer cb_live_...` header also works). The key acts as your user: links it creates belong to you, use your custom domains, and show up in your dashboard.

```
X-API-Key: cb_live_...
```

Set the `api_key` variable in your Postman environment and every request in this collection is ready to run.

## Quick start: send a trackable link

`POST {{base_url}}/api/v1/utm/generate` with `{"base_url": "https://your-site.com/offer"}` → the response's `short_url` is ready to share. Every visit is tracked (geo, device, company intent) and visible in analytics.

## Bring your own domain

1. `POST /api/v1/domains` with your hostname (e.g. `links.acme.com`).
2. Point a DNS **CNAME** for that hostname at the target shown in `GET /api/v1/domains/config` (`cname_target`).
3. ChampBeam verifies DNS and issues the SSL certificate automatically — the domain flips to `active` within ~2 minutes (poll `POST /api/v1/domains/{id}/refresh` or just wait).
4. Pass the domain's `id` as `domain_id` when generating links (or set it primary — it becomes the default), and your short links are served from **your** hostname.

## Rate limits

120 requests/minute per API key (429 when exceeded), plus a general 100 requests/minute per source IP.

## Idempotency

`POST /utm/generate` deduplicates: an identical (destination URL + UTM set + domain) for the same user returns the **existing** link rather than minting a duplicate — safe to retry.

item.name: Getting started
item.description: No-auth service endpoints. `GET /health` is also what ChampBeam's own domain verifier calls on your custom hostname.

request.description: Liveness + database connectivity. Returns `{"status": "healthy", "database": "connected"}`.
Service name, version, and links to the interactive OpenAPI docs (`/docs`, `/redoc`).

item.name: Links
item.description: Create and manage trackable short links. The `short_url` in the generate response is the URL you share; every visit is recorded with geo, device and referrer data.

request.description:
The core endpoint. Give it a destination `base_url` plus optional UTM parameters (`utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_content`, `utm_term`), and optionally `project_id` (folder), `preset_id` (saved UTM defaults) or `domain_id` (serve from your own domain).

Response fields:
- `short_url` — the shareable link (`https://<host>/s/<code>`)
- `redirect_url` — same link on the `/r/` path
- `tracked_url` — the destination with UTM parameters appended
- `link_id` — use for analytics and management calls

Without a `domain_id`, links use your primary active domain, falling back to the platform host. Identical URL+UTM+domain combos return the existing link (idempotent).

item.name: Generate link on your custom domain

request.description:
Same as Generate, but pins the link to one of your **active** custom domains — the returned `short_url` is served from that hostname. Returns 404 `Active domain not found` if the domain isn't yours or isn't active yet.

Set the `domain_id` environment variable to one of your active domain ids (see Domains → List domains); this request is skipped in automated runs when it's unset.
Reassign a link to a project (folder), or `null` to unfile it.

Security console for a link. Only fields you send are applied:
- `expires_in_hours` — self-destruct timer (0 clears)
- `max_views` — view cap (0 clears)
- `require_email` — email gate before redirecting (captured leads: see Get link leads)
- `block_vpn` — refuse VPN/anonymizer visitors
- `revoked` — kill switch (true/false)
Current access-control state for a link.
Emails captured by the `require_email` gate on this link.
Download the CSV template for bulk generation: a required `url` column plus optional per-row `utm_*` columns.

formdata.description: CSV with a 'url' column (see Bulk CSV template)

query.description: Optional saved-preset id supplying default UTM values

request.description:
Upload a CSV (multipart field `file`) and get every row back as a persisted, trackable short link. Optional `preset_id` query parameter applies a saved UTM preset as row defaults.

Skipped in automated runs (needs a local file attached).

item.name: Domains (bring your own)
item.description:
Attach your own hostname so short links are served from your domain. Flow: add → point CNAME at `cname_target` (from Config) → ChampBeam auto-verifies DNS and issues the SSL certificate → status `active` → pass its id as `domain_id` when generating links.

Statuses: `pending_cname` (waiting for your DNS) → `pending_ssl` (DNS verified, certificate being issued — usually under 2 minutes) → `active`. `failed` after repeated certificate failures.

request.description: Which domain features this deployment offers, and — crucially — `cname_target`: the hostname your customers point their CNAME records at.
Your domains with status, setup instructions (`cname_target`) and primary flag. Use an `active` domain's `id` as `domain_id` in link generation.

Register a hostname you own (e.g. `links.acme.com`). Returns the domain in `pending_cname` with setup instructions. Your first domain automatically becomes primary. Hostnames are globally unique (409 if already claimed).
Re-runs verification now (DNS check → certificate → reachability). Optional — ChampBeam re-checks pending domains every minute on its own; this exists so a UI can offer a manual refresh.
Make an **active** domain the default for new links (used when no `domain_id` is passed to generate). Skipped in automated runs when `domain_id` is unset.

item.name: Projects
item.description: Folders for organizing links and files. Pass a project's `id` as `project_id` when generating links.

request.description: Projects with per-project link counts and total clicks.
Deletes the folder; links inside it are unfiled, not deleted.

item.name: Files
item.description:
Host a file (PDF, HTML, image, video…) behind a trackable short link — ideal for sending decks and creative plans. Three-step upload:

1. **Init** — `POST /api/v1/files` with filename/type/size → returns `file_id`, `short_code` and an upload URL.
2. **Upload bytes** — `PUT` the raw bytes to the upload URL (no auth header; the URL is pre-signed).
3. **Finalize** — `POST /api/v1/files/{file_id}/finalize` → returns the shareable `serve_url`.

Like links, file views are tracked (geo, device, per-page reading time for documents) and files support the same access controls (email gate, view caps, expiry, revoke).

request.description: Declares the file. `size_bytes` must match what you'll upload. Optional `domain_id` serves the file link from your custom domain. Response's `presigned_put_url` is where step 2 PUTs the bytes (origin-relative for this deployment: prepend the API origin).

body.raw: Hello from the ChampBeam API docs

request.description: PUT the raw file bytes to the URL from step 1. Send the same `Content-Type` you declared; no API key needed (the URL itself is signed and single-purpose).
Verifies the uploaded bytes and activates the link. The response's `serve_url` is the shareable trackable URL (`https://<host>/f/<code>`).

body.raw: Hello again — updated by the ChampBeam API docs (v2)

request.description:
Replace a file's bytes while keeping its link: `short_code`, serve URL and QR code stay **exactly the same**, so a link you've already emailed now serves the new version. Send the new bytes as the raw body with the correct `Content-Type`. The swap is atomic — the old version keeps serving until the new bytes have fully landed — and view history is preserved.

Perfect for pages/documents you revise on a schedule (weekly plan, live dashboard, price sheet).
Your hosted files with view counts and serve URLs.
Lightweight polling endpoint: view count, last viewed, seen flag.
Aggregate engagement for the file: views, unique viewers, read-through metrics for paginated documents.

item.name: Pages (Beam Pages: hosted, tracked HTML)
item.description: Publish a single-file HTML page behind a permanent trackable link at /p/{slug}. Every open records geo, device, a first-party visitor id, revisits and dwell time; the stored file is served byte-identical with a tracking snippet injected per response. Update in place forever (versions + rollback), optional access code, kill switch, and Beam State (comments + shared key-value state) built in. 2 MB cap; server-side code is rejected.

request.description: One call: send the HTML, get back `url` (`/p/{slug}`). `slug` is optional (derived from the title); `domain_id` serves it from your custom domain.

What recipients hit. Returns the HTML with the tracking snippet in <head>, sets the `cb_vid` visitor cookie, and records a geo/device-enriched view. Also exposes `window.__BEAM__` (state token) and `window.beam`.
Page metadata, counters and current version.
Your pages, newest first.
Atomic content swap; URL/slug/QR unchanged; retained as a new version.

item.name: Change settings (slug / title / enabled / access code)

request.description: Any subset of: `slug` (409 if taken), `title`, `enabled` (false = 410 kill switch), `domain_id`, `access_code` (4–8 digits, null clears).
Retained versions, newest first; `current` marks the live one.
Makes an older version current, recorded as a new version so history stays linear.
Views, unique visitors, revisits, total/median/avg dwell for the window.
Merged timeline: view / revisit / comment_added / state_changed / gate_failed.

item.name: Beam State (public, page-token auth)
item.description: Comments + shared key-value state for a hosted page, so checklists/boards need no external backend. These are the routes `window.beam` calls from inside the page; here they're exercised directly with the page's public token (captured by 'Open the page' above). Same-origin with the page; 410 on every route once the page is disabled.

request.description: Last-writer-wins JSON value (any JSON; 16 KB cap, 200 keys per page).
Every key for the page.
Append-only (4000 chars). Fires a `comment_added` event into the page timeline.
Ascending; pass `after=<comment id>` to poll for newer ones.
The token only ever addresses its own page.

item.name: Analytics
item.description: Everything a click or file view records — geography (city/country), device, referrer, UTM attribution, company intent — queryable per link, per campaign, or account-wide. All time windows accept `days` (default 30) or explicit `start_date`/`end_date` (ISO 8601).

request.description: Account-wide totals: tracked links, clicks, unique visitors, top sources.
Clicks grouped by a UTM dimension. Optional `project_id`/`project_name` filters.
Every tracked link with click and unique-visitor counts — also the way to enumerate your links and their `link_id`s.
The raw click stream for one link: timestamp, city/country, device, browser, referrer, VPN flag.
Clicks bucketed by country and city for one link.
Device / browser / OS split for one link.

Per-campaign rollups (links, clicks, uniques). Drill in via `/campaigns/{campaign_name}`, `/campaigns/{name}/geo`, `/devices`, `/links`, `/timeline`, or compare with `/campaigns/compare?campaigns=a,b`.

query.description: ISO timestamp; only clicks after this moment

request.description: Near-real-time click feed for notifications: poll with `since` set to your last seen timestamp.
Full click-event export as CSV. Also available: `/export/campaign-summary` and `/export/link-performance`.

item.name: QR code for a short link

request.description: Renders an SVG QR code for any URL — point it at a `short_url` and scans are tracked exactly like clicks (there is no separate QR tracking; the QR simply encodes the permanent short link, so it never breaks). Hotlinkable, no auth.

item.name: API key management (Clerk session only)
item.description: Managing keys requires an interactive sign-in (Clerk session Bearer token) — **API keys cannot mint or revoke keys** (403), so a leaked key can't escalate. Normally you do this in the app UI (Settings → API keys); these endpoints exist for completeness. To try them here, set `clerk_session_token` (grab one from the app: DevTools → `await window.Clerk.session.getToken()`). Note Clerk session tokens expire after ~1 minute.

request.description: Your keys: name, display prefix, created / last-used timestamps. Full key values are never shown again after creation.
Returns the full `api_key` (`cb_live_...`) **once** — store it in your secret manager. Limit: 10 active keys.
Immediately kills the key (requests using it 401 from the next call). Revoked keys stay listed for the audit trail.

item.name: Public link behavior (reference)
item.description: What recipients hit when they open your links. No auth — these are the public serving paths. `/s/` and `/r/` redirect to the destination and record the click; `/f/` streams a hosted file and records the view. All are Host-aware: on a custom domain, only that owner's codes resolve.

request.description: 302 → the tracked destination. This is the path `short_url` uses.
Same link on the `/r/` path (`redirect_url` in the generate response). Email-gated or revoked links render an interstitial instead of redirecting.
Streams the hosted file (or renders the viewer for documents) and records the view with geo + device.

item.name: Cleanup (demo data)
item.description: Deletes the objects created by running this collection, so repeat runs stay tidy. Safe to skip.

request.description: Deleting a link also removes its click history. The short code stops resolving.
Refuses (409) if links were generated on the domain; pass `?force=true` to delete anyway.
Removes the page and every version blob; the URL 404s immediately.
